analysis.title: Few charts to end the week
key_insights: Yesterday (22 Oct) was the 5th largest hedge fund de-grossing event this year per GS prime brokerage data, driven entirely by long selling. It was the largest long selling since September 2025.
Gross exposure remains elevated while net leverage continues to come down.
Allocation to Semi & Semi equipment among hedge funds has come down substantially.
The US momentum factor has given back all of its gains for this year. Cyclicals vs Defensives has followed a similar pattern and has been weak with the momentum sell-off.
The capex super-cycle is intensifying competition for capital while interest rates are higher, so the cost of capital keeps rising.
Tech is no longer capital-light. US hyperscalers' operating cash flow is becoming insufficient to fund capex, which raises their reliance on external financing.
Leverage remains low compared to the broader market, for both Europe overall and the European Tech sector.
Other things equal, a 100bp increase in the cost of debt would knock off 3% of STOXX 600 earnings.
Interest expense as a % of sales in Europe is rising as the interest burden intensifies, and Net Debt to EBITDA has started to pick up.
Since 2022, refinancing rates have moved above the coupon paid on already issued debt (iBoxx Euro Corporate).
3Q-26 earnings surprises are slightly below the historical average. Analysts expect 24% STOXX 600 EPS growth in H2, and 15% excluding commodities.
earnings_insights: 3Q-26 earnings surprise (equal weighted, STOXX 600) is slightly below the historical average.
Analysts expect 24% y/y EPS growth for the STOXX 600 in H2 (consensus expectation, not a reported figure), and 15% excluding commodities.
risk_factors: Rising cost of capital as the capex super-cycle competes for funding while interest rates are higher.
US hyperscalers' operating cash flow is insufficient to fund capex, increasing reliance on external financing.
A 100bp rise in the cost of debt would reduce STOXX 600 earnings by about 3%.
Rising interest burden and Net Debt to EBITDA in Europe.
Continued weakness in the momentum factor and further hedge fund de-grossing.
charts_described: Momentum vs. Market (MSCI indices): momentum has given back all its gains this year.
Interest expenses as a % of Sales in Europe vs. the Corporate IG Yield: the interest burden is intensifying.
EPS sensitivity to a 100bp increase in the cost of debt: about 3% of STOXX 600 earnings.
vol_and_positioning: 22 Oct was the 5th largest hedge fund de-grossing event of the year, driven entirely by long selling, the largest long selling since September 2025.
Net exposure continues to come down while gross exposure is rising and remains elevated.

The US momentum factor has given back all of its gains this year.
